title: Open direct-image dimension on arbitrary curves
statement: Let $k$ be a finite field or its algebraic closure, let $T$ be a scheme of finite type over $k$ [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] whose underlying topological space has Krull dimension at most one [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension], and let $j:U\hookrightarrow T$ be any open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion]. Let $A$ be a finite commutative ring killed by a power of a prime $\ell$ invertible on $T$. Then $R^qj_*M=0$ for every integer $q>1$ and every etale $A$-module sheaf $M$ on $U$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves], with higher direct images as in [def-weil-pbc-direct-image].

proof.text: Fix $M$ and $q>1$, and let $F$ be the underlying abelian sheaf of $M$. Since $\ell^n A=0$ for some $n$, $\ell^n F=0$, so $F$ is torsion. Apply clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-exchange-forget-coefficients] to the cartesian square with vertical arrows $j,j$ and horizontal identity arrows, and to $M[0]$. Taking degree-$q$ cohomology, using the exactness of scalar-forgetting explicitly stated there, identifies the underlying abelian sheaf of $R^qj_*M$ with $R^qj_*F$. This comparison is stated for modules over the constant ring sheaf, the coefficient category used in the theorem. It therefore suffices to prove that this abelian sheaf is zero. The field spectrum is Noetherian, so [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] makes $T$ Noetherian. By [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-open-subscheme-noetherian], every open subscheme of $T$, including the intersection of $U$ with any affine open of $T$, is quasi-compact. This proves that $j$ is quasi-compact. Its diagonal is an isomorphism, since an open immersion identifies $U$ with an open subscheme [def-weil-open-immersion]; hence $j$ is also quasi-separated.

source.place: Tag 0D6J (lemma-modules-abelian-unbounded), part (3); morphisms.tex Tag 01T6; properties.tex Tags 01OW, 01OZ

proof.text: For every geometric point $\bar t$ of $T$, [prop-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-stalk-formula] now applies to the qcqs morphism $j$ and the torsion sheaf $F$. Write $R=\mathcal O^{\mathrm{sh}}_{T,\bar t}$, $V=U\times_T\operatorname{Spec}R$, and $F_V$ for the pullback of $F$. It gives $(R^qj_*F)_{\bar t}\cong H^q(V,F_V)$. Choose an affine finite-type $k$-chart $\operatorname{Spec}B$ containing $t$. Let $\mathfrak p$ be the prime of $t$ in $B$ and let $K$ be the separable closure of $\kappa(t)$ selected by $\bar t$. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-local-ring-triples], $R$, defined by affine pointed neighbourhoods, is canonically the colimit of etale residue triples over $(B,\mathfrak p,K)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-triples], this colimit is the algebraic strict henselization of $B_{\mathfrak p}=\mathcal O_{T,t}$, is strictly henselian, has residue field $K$, and the preimage of its maximal ideal in $B$ is $\mathfrak p$. Thus its closed point maps to $t$. By [lem-sc-strict-henselization-dimension], $\dim R=\dim\mathcal O_{T,t}\le1$: a prime chain in $B_{\mathfrak p}$ is a prime chain in $B$, and the closures in $T$ of the corresponding points are a strict chain of irreducible closed subsets, bounded in length by the hypothesis on $T$.

If $t\in U$, every point of $\operatorname{Spec}R$ maps into $U$: the preimage of $U$ is an open containing the closed point of this local spectrum, and an open containing its maximal ideal contains a basic open $D(f)$ with $f$ a unit, hence is the whole spectrum. Thus $V=\operatorname{Spec}R$, and [lem-weil-pbc-strictly-henselian-etale-acyclic] gives $H^q(V,F_V)=0$ because $q>1$.

Suppose $t\notin U$. The closed point of $\operatorname{Spec}R$ is absent from $V$. If $\dim R=0$, this is its only point: every prime of a zero-dimensional local ring equals its maximal ideal. Hence $V$ is empty. An abelian sheaf on the empty scheme is zero by the empty covering axiom, so its cohomology vanishes. Otherwise $\dim R=\dim\mathcal O_{T,t}=1$. This forces $t$ to be closed in $T$. Indeed there is a strict generization $s$ of $t$ from a strict prime chain in its local ring; if $t$ had a distinct specialization $z$, then $\overline{\{z\}}\subsetneq\overline{\{t\}}\subsetneq\overline{\{s\}}$ would contradict $\dim T\le1$. The closures are irreducible, and strictness follows from the $T_0$ property of scheme spaces. This also covers an isolated zero-dimensional component of $T$, without assuming that $U$ is dense.

source.place: Proof, first paragraph (generic points) and second paragraph (dimension-zero case), with the prime-chain argument written out

proof.text: In the remaining case $t$ is closed. By [lem-kun-closed-point-field], $\kappa(t)$ is finite over $k$. It is therefore a finite field if $k$ is finite, and equals $k$ if $k$ is algebraically closed. In either case its separable closure is algebraically closed of characteristic $p=\operatorname{char}k$: in the finite-field case every finite subextension of the separable closure is itself a finite field, whose Frobenius is bijective, so their union is perfect; a polynomial irreducible over this perfect, separably closed union must be linear, since a zero derivative would make it a $p$-th power. In the algebraically closed case the separable closure is the field itself. Together with the residue-field description in step 2 this gives the algebraically closed residue field required below. By [lem-exc-field-algebra-strict-henselization-excellent], $R$ and $R_0=R/\sqrt{(0)}$ are excellent and Noetherian. The quotient $R_0$ is henselian by [lem-weil-pbc-quotient-henselian-pair], and has the same residue field and prime spectrum as $R$; thus it is reduced, one-dimensional and strictly henselian. By [lem-weil-pbc-reduction-universal-homeomorphism] its spectrum maps to $\operatorname{Spec}R$ by a universal homeomorphism. The same holds for the reduction of $V$, namely $V_0=V\times_{\operatorname{Spec}R}\operatorname{Spec}R_0$. By [thm-weil-pbc-universal-homeomorphism-invariance], pullback identifies $H^q(V,F_V)$ with $H^q(V_0,F_0)$, where $F_0$ retains its pulled-back $A$-action.

source.place: Proof, second paragraph; supporting Stacks Tags 07QT, 07QU, 07QW, 09XK, 054M, 04DY, 04DZ; strict-henselization excellence is isolated as a new unsplit algebra lemma

proof.text: Apply [lem-exc-punctured-curve-branches] to $R_0$. All its hypotheses were established in step 5, and its punctured spectrum is a finite disjoint union $\coprod_{a=1}^r\operatorname{Spec}K_a$, with each $K_a$ the fraction field of an excellent strictly henselian DVR with that same algebraically closed residue field of characteristic $p$. Since $V_0$ is an open missing the closed point, it is an open of this punctured spectrum. Each $\operatorname{Spec}K_a$ is a single point, so its intersection with $V_0$ is either empty or the whole summand. Consequently $V_0$ is the coproduct over a subset $J\subseteq\{1,\ldots,r\}$ of these fields, with $J$ finite, possibly empty.

source.place: Proof, second paragraph, final sentence; branch algebra input as in Stacks Tags 0C3S, 00PD (as cited by the branch lemma)

proof.text: Fix $a\in J$ and put $X_a=\operatorname{Spec}K_a$. Let $M_a$ be the restriction of the pulled-back $A$-module sheaf to $X_a$, with underlying abelian sheaf $F_a=F_0|_{X_a}$. By [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaf-constant-ring-equivalence], choose an equivalence $E_a$ from module-valued sheaves to modules over the constant ring sheaf, retaining the underlying additive sheaf. Evaluating its natural isomorphism at the final etale object $X_a$ gives a natural isomorphism of additive section functors. The equivalence is additive because it preserves finite biproducts, and is exact and carries injective resolutions to injective resolutions by [lem-weil-pbc-equivalence-injective-resolutions]. The constant-ring-sheaf module category has enough injectives by [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-enough-injectives]; the inverse equivalence and the same resolution lemma give enough injectives in the module-valued category. Apply [lem-exc-equivalence-derived-sections] to these section functors, valued in abelian groups. Thus the underlying section-cohomology groups in the two encodings agree in every degree. This uses only a fixed field spectrum.

source.place: Tag 015M, lemma-compose-derived-functors, exact-equivalence case; blueprint Proof paragraph 3, first sentence

proof.text: Put $G_a=\operatorname{Gal}(K_a^{\mathrm{sep}}/K_a)$ and let $N_a$ be the geometric fibre of the module sheaf on $X_a$. By [lem-exc-field-discrete-modules], geometric fibre is an exact equivalence to discrete continuous $A[G_a]$-modules and carries sections to invariants. These categories have enough injectives by [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-enough-injectives] and [lem-exc-discrete-modules-abelian]. Apply [lem-exc-equivalence-derived-sections] to sections and invariants, with values in $\operatorname{Mod}(A)$. By [def-exc-continuous-cohomology], the latter derived functors are $H^q(G_a,N_a)$. Combining this comparison with the preceding encoding comparison and [lem-weil-pbc-etale-module-cohomology-forget] identifies the underlying additive group of $H^q(G_a,N_a)$ with $H^q(X_a,F_a)$. No finiteness assumption on the module $N_a$ has been introduced.

source.place: Tag 015M, lemma-compose-derived-functors, exact-equivalence case; blueprint Proof paragraph 3, first sentence

proof.text: Each $K_a$ is the fraction field of an excellent strictly henselian DVR with algebraically closed residue field of characteristic $p$, by step 6. In this remaining case $t\in T$, so $T$ is nonempty. Invertibility of $\ell$ on $T$ implies $\ell\ne p$, since its image in $\kappa(t)$ is a unit. The ring $A$ is finite and killed by a power of $\ell$. Hence [lem-exc-dvr-galois] gives $H^q(G_a,N_a)=0$ for $q>1$ and every $a\in J$. The comparison of the preceding step yields $H^q(X_a,F_a)=0$.

source.place: Proof paragraph 3, second sentence: apply the DVR computation to each branch field

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-coproduct-cohomology-assembly], $H^q(V_0,F_0)$ is the finite product of the zero groups from step 9, hence zero (including the empty product). Steps 3–9 give $H^q(V,F_V)=0$ at every geometric point. The stalk isomorphism in step 2 therefore shows that all geometric stalks of $R^qj_*F$ vanish. Apply [lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative] to its morphism to the zero sheaf to conclude $R^qj_*F=0$. The scalar-forgetting comparison in step 1 now gives $R^qj_*M=0$, since a module sheaf with zero underlying abelian sheaf is zero. If $T$ is empty, its only module sheaf is zero and this last conclusion already holds.
